DOAC (Direct Oral Anticoagulants) is a group of medications used in the [[atrieflimren-behandling|treatment of atrial fibrillation]] in Denmark. As a modern form of [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]], DOACs are prescribed to [[praevalente-patienter-med-atrieflimren|prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation]] to prevent complications such as ischemic stroke, while aiming to minimize bleeding risks compared to older therapies like [[marevan|marevan]] [^src1] [^src2] [^src6]. The national quality database, [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]], closely monitors the safety, efficacy, and clinical management of patients receiving these drugs [^src5] [^src7].

The specific medications classified under DOAC include [[b01ae07|B01AE07]] (dabigatran), [[b01af01|B01AF01]] (rivaroxaban), [[b01af02|B01AF02]] (apixaban), and [[b01af03|B01AF03]] (edoxaban) [^src15]. Because these drugs are processed through the kidneys, clinical guidelines mandate regular monitoring of renal function. Specifically, [[indikator-4b|Indicator 4b]] measures the proportion of patients on DOAC who receive at least one annual measurement of [[s-creatinin|S-creatinin]] or [[npu04998-p-kreatinin|P-creatinin]] [^src5] [^src6] [^src15]. Nationally, 93.9% of the prevalent patient population on DOAC met this monitoring standard, reflecting strong adherence to safety protocols [^src7].

A major focus of the pharmacovigilance surrounding DOAC is its safety profile regarding bleeding events. According to the annual reports, the introduction of DOAC is expected to reduce the risk of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|intracranial bleeding]] over time compared to marevan [^src2]. In the 2023 reporting period, the proportion of patients experiencing intracranial bleeding was 0.52% for DOAC and 0.46% for marevan [^src1], while in the 2024 report, the rate was 0.53% for DOAC and 0.82% for marevan [^src9]. Similarly, the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|severe bleeding]] (tracked under indicators like [[indikator-7|Indicator 7]]) was slightly lower for DOAC (2.30% - 2.33%) compared to marevan (2.38% - 2.44%) [^src3] [^src10]. 

Furthermore, the prevention of ischemic stroke is tracked via [[indikator-5|Indicator 5]]. The data shows that the proportion of patients suffering an ischemic stroke was 0.89% for DOAC and 0.51% for marevan [^src8]. For patients receiving neither DOAC nor marevan, the rate of ischemic stroke was 0.53% [^src4]. The safety of anticoagulation is also evaluated through [[indikator-6|Indicator 6]], which specifically compares the treatment effects and bleeding risks across different patient demographics and risk profiles [^src9]. Overall, DOAC represents a critical, closely monitored component of cardiovascular healthcare in Denmark, balancing stroke prevention with the mitigation of severe bleeding risks.
